scope.newlyReviewedScience: Complete changed case-2 DE/EN task, explicitly supplied fictional materials, expected performance, assessment method, four criteria, full-credit evidence, misconceptions and provenance.
scope.retainedScience: The prior sealed acceptance of case-1 remains informed background. Its whole object is independently checked equal to the original; it is not newly rewritten or presented as a new case review.
scope.wholeProfileApplicability: Original aspect-1/aspect-2 expectations and variation/coverage rules are read for applicability of the exact new pair. The old profile object remains untouched and still embeds the incomplete original case-2.

missingMaterialResolved.before: The old demand invoked supplied/measured solubility observations but did not actually supply observations, comparison amount or temperature. Its expected answer could not supply those missing data.
missingMaterialResolved.after: Both language materials now explicitly supply two fictional qualitative results at maintained pH: visible solid remains at pH 3.0; no solid is visible at pH 8.0. Each separate mixture contains 1.00 g of the same crystalline L-glutamic acid in 100 mL final aqueous mixture at 20 °C after modeled equilibrium.
missingMaterialResolved.conclusion: The learner can now compare given observations without inventing data. These are stated author model observations, not observations of a real learner or actual experiment.

chemicalCorrectness: A carboxyl-containing acidic side chain remains the same covalent side-chain type when the protonation state changes. Calling its group acidic is compatible with predominantly COOH at pH 3 and COO− at pH 8.

Under the stipulated pKa model, at pH 3 the dominant alpha COO−/NH3+/side COOH form has formal net charge 0. The independently recomputed ratios 6.3096 and 0.05012 show appreciable mixtures and do not justify exclusive protonation.
At pH 8 the dominant alpha COO−/NH3+/side COO− form has formal net charge −1. NH2/NH3+ is approximately 0.01995, so the ammonium group is predominantly protonated and is not 100 percent protonated.

Increased negative charge and changed water interactions can plausibly contribute to greater dissolved loading at pH 8. The rubric correctly asks for a plausible contribution and retains counterion, ionic-strength and lattice limits. It does not isolate side-chain polarity as the sole cause.

The stated 10 g/L total loading is not a numerical saturation solubility. A qualitative solid/no-solid comparison does not provide an exact saturation concentration; the new task and rubric explicitly prevent that overclaim.

Free-amino-acid comparison is not a universal protein-position rule or a statement that all nonpolar-side-chain amino acids are absolutely water-insoluble. The stated limits preserve that distinction.
case2ScientificJudgment.DEENAndRubricReview: Both language demands and materials present the same mass, final volume, temperature, pH values, qualitative observations, model pKa values and uncontrolled matrix limitations. Both expected performances and full-credit texts distinguish dominant forms from exclusive forms. The four 1-point criteria require classification/form reasoning, an actual comparison of both given observations, a bounded charge/hydration explanation, and rejection of numerical or universal overclaims. The task supports those criteria from material supplied to the learner.
case2ScientificJudgment.transferReview: The second case varies the same glutamic-acid side-chain type across pH and requires distinguishing covalent identity, protonation, whole-species charge and bounded observable outcome. This extends the unchanged case-1 leucine/lysine residue comparison without making a universal single-factor solubility inference.
case2ScientificJudgment.acquisitionAndEvidenceBoundary: The current b47 goal asks classification and explanation of observable properties; it does not demand that this learner carry out the experiment. Supplied fictional observations are therefore sufficient data for this design. A future real practical execution or real solubility determination would need its own protocol, measured data and controls. A model answer is not learner performance.

wholeProfileApplicability.conclusion: The exact successor pair is scientifically adequate for the existing two-aspect b47 concept-profile design, within E1/G1. This resolves the previously recorded missing-material defect for a future exact binding to this successor pair.
wholeProfileApplicability.aspect1: The unchanged case-1 retains the accepted leucine/lysine comparison and whole-molecule/shared-ionisable-group limit. No new case-1 evidence or learner trial is claimed.
wholeProfileApplicability.aspect2: The corrected case-2 now supplies the observations previously presupposed by aspect-2. Its pH variation probes how the same side-chain type changes protonation/charge and how limited the property inference remains.
wholeProfileApplicability.coverageAndVariation: Two distinct design opportunities remain: residue comparison across leucine/lysine and pH-dependent transfer for glutamic acid. The profile can require two independent demonstrations and fresh variation at delivery. This is a capacity of the design, not proof that a learner has completed either demonstration or that any future generated variation is already reviewed.
wholeProfileApplicability.currentContextFit: The unchanged selected goal requires atomic e9d34f34-2a43-5cc7-bcca-1d08e057531d, whose whole description covers pH-dependent amino-acid charge and amphoteric acid/base reasoning. The whole goal, requires, image and source mappings are unchanged by this correction.

scientificFindings.finding: The learner material now explicitly distinguishes observed alpha = +5.3 degrees from SPECIFIC reference [alpha] values +52.7 and -92.4 degree mL/(g dm). It supplies the alpha = [alpha]lc convention and explicitly denies that the references are observed angles at the stated path/concentration. This directly resolves the original quantity ambiguity without relying on the model answer as missing task data.

With l = 1.00 dm and c = 0.100 g/mL, the independent calculation is +53 degree mL/(g dm). The denominator carries dm*g/mL, so the resulting quantity has the same units as both explicit references. The coefficient comparison is now dimensionally and conceptually valid.

Holding l and c fixed, the supplied angular uncertainty +/-0.1 degrees propagates linearly to +/-1 degree mL/(g dm), yielding [52,54] in the model. The glucose reference +52.7 lies inside it and fructose -92.4 lies far outside. Independently predicted observed angles are +5.27 and -9.24 degrees. This is a comparison under the stipulated model, not a metrologically complete uncertainty statement.

The material supplies water, 20 degrees C, 589 nm, purity and an assumed comparison equilibrium state. The model answer also names concentration convention and equilibrium as constraints. Those assumptions support the restricted reference comparison and avoid silently treating an arbitrary initial anomer state as the same reference equilibrium.

Only glucose and fructose are allowed candidates in the fictional pure-sample model. Glucose is therefore the compatible stipulated candidate; a matching single specific rotation would not identify an arbitrary unknown substance or mixture uniquely. Positive optical rotation does not establish D configuration, and the task/answer explicitly demand that limit.
